Without access to the newest, most powerful cyber-capable models, companies would fall behind in finding and remediating vulnerabilities. The assumption was understandable. Finding vulnerabilities at scale is hard, and the strongest model would surely deliver the strongest security results. Access to it, many believed, would determine who stayed ahead. Our security research added an important nuance. Models matter, but their real value also depends on the harness around them, the skills, workflows and business context baked in from the start. articles.excerpt: Merchants who let AI agents act autonomously should first assign responsibility for mistakes or extreme risks. “Once an agent can update a product catalog, issue a refund, or change a campaign, it becomes operational software with delegated business authority. The company needs to treat it that way,” wrote David Greenberg, chief marketing officer at BlueRock Security , a cybersecurity company. Businesses, including ecommerce shops, are evolving from experimenting with AI to deploying agents in production or customer-facing applications. Consider an ecommerce merchant that instructs an AI agent to improve conversion rates for underperforming products. The agent might examine inventory, identify slow-selling items, reduce prices, and shift advertising spending toward those products. Each action could be reasonable, but the combined result might undermine margins, exhaust inventory, or create unexpected costs. The question then is how much authority the merchant should delegate. The Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s Center for Information Systems Research identified two factors — ambiguity and risk — to determine which decisions AI should make. Routine tasks with predictable outcomes and limited consequences are good candidates for automation. But matters involving uncertainty, significant financial exposure, or competing objectives warrant greater human involvement. The e-commerce giant said select U.S. customers will get a text asking them to enable the shopping feature. Those with access can text Alexa to shop on Amazon using natural language queries, spanning everything from searching for items, adding them to cart, and purchasing. The text agent builds on the recent shopping-focused upgrades to Alexa , and so can manage lists, keep tabs on prices, search for items across the web, compare products, and check the status of orders. Users can also share a picture of an item or someone wearing an outfit to search for similar listings on Amazon. The company said over time, Alexa will learn users’ preferences and suggest items accordingly. The company said users who don’t get invited to use this feature can sign up to a waitlist . The feature will be rolled out more broadly in the coming weeks. As the market for consumer-focused AI agents balloons, platforms like Amazon are building their own to tap this new avenue of user interaction. Not being ready for every agent is not the same as being absent from AI. The largest retailers are doing deals with one or two assistants instead of opening their doors to all of them. This to me is like saying you’ll sell on Debenhams and Amazon, but refuse to engage with eBay, Argos, Tesco and all of the other big marketplaces. You can’t do Agentic Commerce and block most of the assistants…. not unless you have supreme confidence that your shoppers all use the same agent! This is the first Black Friday where lots of people will ask an assistant to find the deal and buy it. If your site turns that assistant away, you don’t get a second chance. The shopper buys from whoever let it in. America’s biggest brands have every right to be guarded, and the new protocols let them do that and still sell. The ones doing neither risk being forgotten, and their competitors, whether they’re down the street or overseas, will happily take their place. Ceconomy exploite 1 067 magasins dans 11 pays européens , notamment sous les enseignes MediaMarkt et Saturn. Le distributeur réalise environ 23 milliards d’euros de chiffre d’affaires, dont 5,7 milliards d’euros via le e-commerce . Le groupe avait déjà renforcé sa présence en Europe avec le lancement de Joybuy en France en mars 2026 .
